transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question! You should avoid any exercise for the first week after surgery. But after that week, you can go back to light exercise like gardening.

So you'd be able to start gentle gardening from about a week onwards.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, thank you. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you can go ahead and use it as you were before.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It is quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. 

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you have significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity - especially if your eye is also red and painful - that's not normal, and we may need to check that further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry now, or if it's getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text:
It was about two weeks ago. I guess I was just wondering if some blurriness is still normal at this point. 

Thank you for providing all this information. I have no more questions for now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You're welcome! At two weeks, some mild blurriness can still be normal as your eyes continue to settle. But if it's getting worse or you're concerned, do let us know.

Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and remember to wear those sunglasses outside!

verdict.label: pass
